title: setValidityState doesn't work correctly on tab removal page
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
Participant 1
comments.body:
Hi @Trinetra-MSFT Thx for response.  

> Teams enables the Remove button after 5 seconds, even if your tab hasn't called setValidityState().

This is very strange. 5 seconds is a very short time. What's the point of having app's call setValidityState if it will have no effect after 5 seconds?

I get that you probably want to allow end users to remove Tab regardless of app logic (like in case of app error). However, I feel either: 
1. That there should be an alternative mechanism for end user to hard remove tab
2. Or, the documentation should not recommend app developers to call `setValidityState` as its confusing and has no ultimate effect. 
3. Or, There should be a longer timeout to enable the remove button. 

Thx for your consideration

comments.author: Participant 2
Participant 1
Participant 3
comments.body: @synth, removing an app doesn’t actually cause all the tabs to be removed. They are simply hidden and get re-shown if/when the app is installed into the team again.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
Thanks for letting us know this. Is there documentation on this? Seems problematic. Companies will expect that uninstalling an app hard deletes all data. Imagine one user adds the app and installs several tabs. That user ends up leaving the org and the app is subsequently uninstalled. Then another user later installs the app...then all of the previous tabs are restored unbeknownst to the current user. In a team with a lot of channels, it would be near impossible to manage - let alone the compliance issues with the 3rd party app holding onto data it shouldn't (if the app is uninstalled).

There should be a full app uninstall hook that notifies the app to clean up all of its component references and data.

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body: @synth, thank you for the feedback. We are aware of the asks for an app/tab removal hook and is something we will be looking into. It’s important to keep in mind that tabs in and of themselves do not store any data; they are just pointers to external sites which store the data (not that different from contextually relevant bookmarks). Data access, compliance, and retention policies need to be handled by the external sites. You should not be relying on Teams to do that for you.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: Thanks @ydogandjiev. It's good to know an app removal hook is on your radar. It's true the tab itself doesn't store any data, and it's us, as third parties, that are storing data. This is precisely the reason for a need for an app removal hook. In other words, the app removal hook can help 3rd parties to clean out data that should no longer be stored which follows international compliance requirements (gdpr, ccpa, etc).

comments.author: Participant 3
comments.body: Hi @synth, thank you for takin the time to report this issue. The specific behavior of setValidityState that you have described is by design. We do not want to allow app developers to intentionally or accidentally block users from being able to delete their tabs. That is why we automatically enable the "Remove" button after 5 seconds and allow the user to force delete the tab.
